items.title: What's at stake for Paramount, the Ellisons in Warner Bros. takeover bid
items.summary: Paramount Skydance (PSKY) is facing some pushback from a collection of US attorneys general in its proposed acquisition of rival Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). Evan Shapiro — better known as "The Media Cartographer" — comes on Market Domination Overtime to outline what is it at stake for the media giant and the Ellison family if the deal ultimately falls through.

items.title: Google’s Wins Make Founders Brin And Page $50 Billion Richer
items.summary: While AI was supposed to gut Google's core business and rivals like Meta and Tesla have stumbled badly this year, Alphabet's founders are sitting on a jaw-dropping windfall that tells a very different story.

items.title: Netflix Rises 3% on a $95 Wolfe Research Price Target, Leaving Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery Behind
items.summary: Wolfe Research says Netflix's rough summer had nothing to do with demand, and that one reframing sent shares jumping while Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery barely flinched. Here is what the analyst actually found buried in millions of viewing data points.

items.title: The Retail Silence That Reshapes The Amazon Stock Bull Case
items.summary: Management's narrative has pivoted hard from optimizing its massive retail machine to funding aggressive AI infrastructure buildouts, quietly changing what an investment in the company is actually a bet on.

items.title: The Price of Progress for Google Stock
items.summary: If you hold Alphabet (GOOGL) stock, the recent top-line numbers look spectacular. In the second quarter of 2026, the company delivered 24% overall revenue growth, propelled by an 82% surge in its Google Cloud segment. This is the AI-fueled future investors have been waiting for. But beneath the surface of that growth, a fundamental shift is underway in the company’s financial DNA, and it represents the most significant risk to the stock today.

items.title: Netflix engagement data points to stronger results ahead, Wolfe says
items.summary: Investing.com -- Wolfe Research has lifted its price target on Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) to $95 from $84, telling clients in a note that its analysis of viewing data suggests the streamer's soft second quarter was a scheduling issue rather than a demand problem.
